notes: Built on lane/gap-svc-status. DECISION (the lead's default, the owner is away): the status is THIS MAC'S OWN connection state per mail service; no status page is fetched and no network call exists (the rule 'nothing leaves this Mac except the relay'). Swift: Sources/Features/SettingsAccountsMac/ServiceStatus.swift (MailService, ServiceState, ServiceStatusRow), the group in AccountsPaneView.swift (serviceStatus, drawn with SettingsGroup and SettingsRow), the rows registered as mac-settings-accounts.service-status in SettingsAccountsMacFeature.swift (rowSources). An account belongs to a service by the core's detected route (MailProvider); Zoho has no route, so an IMAP account whose host is zoho.* or zohomail.* is Zoho. States: no account on this Mac, Connected, Needs sign-in (a failure with no sync code), Paused (a paused account), Cannot reach the server (a failure that carries a sync code, SyncStatusWords). Proof 0: the case labels par-settingsaccountsmac-services/service-status-<gmail|outlook|icloud|fastmail|zoho>-is-named-with-its-state and five more print one `pass` line each through print_cases; it needs the lead's run on the fixture core. Proof 1: the model selftest, which includes the 8 new cases and one declared broken copy for each. Proof 2: the nine unit tests in Tests/Unit/SettingsAccountsServiceStatusTests.swift, run by the lead. Not proved here: nothing was compiled or run by the builder (the lead compiles and runs the Swift and the hidden check). The selftest judges a Python model of the pane, not the Swift. Already there and not mine: i18n-check --coverage and --catalogue are red on one key, the CSS literal at Sources/Features/MessageBody/MessageBodyPassage.swift:165.
